### Introduction

We study depth-three Boolean OR–AND–OR circuits with arbitrary fan-in and fan-out. Such a circuit is a disjunction of CNFs: conjunctions of clauses, each a disjunction of literals. Classical lower bounds for explicit functions have an exponent proportional to the square root of the input length. We ask whether one polynomial-time language can require more than $2^{A\sqrt n}$ gates for every constant $A>0$, at every sufficiently large length. The word “one” matters: the language and its membership algorithm must be fixed before $A$ is chosen.

Throughout the paper, $S_3(f)$ denotes the minimum *total* number of AND and OR gates in an OR–AND–OR circuit computing $f$ exactly. Every bottom gate and the output gate are counted. Input negations are free. The three layers are successive: bottom gates read literals and optional constants, middle gates read bottom outputs, and the top gate reads middle outputs. Unary gates allow smaller-depth functions in this model.

outputs.exact_statement: There is a language $L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$, a deterministic Turing machine deciding $L$, and fixed positive integers $C,a$ such that the machine runs in time at most $C(n+1)^a$ on every input of length $n$. If $f_n$ is the membership function of $L$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, then $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 S_3(f_n)}{\sqrt n}=\infty.$$ Equivalently, for every real $A>0$, there is an integer $N_A$ such that $$S_3(f_n)>2^{A\sqrt n}\qquad\text{for every }n\ge N_A.$$ No uniformity or bottom fan-in restriction is imposed on the circuits.

For every integer $b\ge 1$ and real $\eta>0$, there is a positive integer $M=M(b,\eta)$ with the following property. Every CNF indicator $H$ of width at most $b$ on $m\ge 1$ variables can be written pointwise as $$H=\sum_{a=1}^{q} H_a,
  \qquad q\le 2^{\eta m},$$ where the $H_a$ are CNF indicators of width at most $b$, each represented by at most $Mm$ clauses, and their satisfying sets are pairwise disjoint. The empty sum is permitted when $H=0$.
Let $s\ge 0$ and $r\ge 2$ be integers. A family of more than $s!(r-1)^s$ distinct sets of cardinality $s$ contains a sunflower with $r$ members.
The language $L$ is decided on every input of length $n$ by one deterministic Turing machine in time $C(n+1)^a$, for some fixed positive integers $C,a$.

For each fixed integer $b\ge1$ and real $B>0$, all sufficiently large lengths $n$ admit fixed settings of the non-data bits such that, with $$p=\frac{B}{\sqrt d},\qquad m_0=pd=B\sqrt d,$$ the resulting sign $g$ satisfies $$\label{eq:good-slices}
 \Pr_{T,\rho}\left[
 |T|\notin[m_0/2,2m_0]
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \mathop{\mathrm{corr}}_b(g_{T,\rho})>2^{-|T|/8}
 \right]
 \le4\cdot2^{-m_0/16}.$$ Here $T$ includes each of the $d$ data coordinates independently with probability $p$, and $\rho$ is an independent uniform assignment outside $T$. In particular, the correlation bound on a good restriction holds simultaneously for all members of $\mathcal C_b(T)$.
For every integer $r\ge1$, there is a monic irreducible polynomial of degree $r$ over $\mathbb F_2$.

coverage.checked_domain: All multiplication instances for r=1,2,3, every monic modulus and all operand residues; all three-coefficient evaluations for r=1,2; selected r=16 boundary evaluations, including zero polynomial and reducible moduli.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact binary carryless multiplication and Horner evaluation compared with direct polynomial powers and exact polynomial remainder in characteristic two. No circuit-bound claim is checked.
